title: Drop the nth stop from the end
statement:
A route is a singly linked list. Remove the `n`th node counting from the end (n = 1 is the last node) and return the head of the changed list. `n` is always between 1 and the length of the list.

Try to do it in a single pass. In tests, a list is written as an array of its values.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Is n always valid?
clarifyingQuestions.why: Lets you skip bounds checks for n.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Can I remove the head?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Yes, when n equals the length.
clarifyingQuestions.why: The most common bug: the head case needs care, solved by a dummy node.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Can I do it in one pass?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: That’s the goal; two passes are fine as a start.

edgeCases.why: Removing the only node returns an empty list.

approaches.name: Two passes
approaches.idea: Count the length L, then walk L - n steps to the node before the target and unlink it.

approaches.name: One pass with a gap
approaches.idea: Move a fast pointer n steps ahead, then move fast and slow together until fast reaches the last node. slow is now just before the target.
approaches.tradeoffs: One pass; needs a dummy head so slow can stop before the head.

optimal.name: Two pointers n apart with a dummy
optimal.explanation: Start fast and slow at a dummy node before head. Advance fast n times. Then advance both until fast.next is None. Set slow.next = slow.next.next and return dummy.next.

hintLadder: Removing a node in a singly linked list needs which node?
Could you find the length first?
What if two pointers kept a fixed distance apart?
Lead with a fast pointer n steps ahead from a dummy head; when it hits the end, the slow one is before the target.

expectedMentions.what: Asks or notes that the head itself may be removed
Proposes pointers n apart for one pass
Uses a dummy node to handle removing the head
Traces removing the head or the only node

followUps: Do it for a doubly linked list.

walkthrough.say: n is always between 1 and the length? So n equal to the length means I remove the head?
The straightforward way is two passes: count the length, then walk to the node before the target. That’s O(n) and fine, but I can do one pass.

If a fast pointer starts n nodes ahead of a slow pointer and they move together, when fast is at the last node, slow is n plus one from the end, the node right before the one to remove. I’ll start both at a dummy node so removing the head works the same way.
Build the gap, then move together.
slow is just before the target, so skip over it.
For 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and n of 2: fast moves to 6. Then both move until fast is 9, and slow is at 7. Unlink 8. Result 5, 6, 7, 9.
For a single node 5 with n of 1: fast moves to 5, fast.next is null so slow stays at dummy, and I unlink 5. dummy.next is null, an empty list. That’s exactly why I needed the dummy.
One pass, O(L) time, O(1) space.
